tess: Heads up — seeing a sawtooth p99 latency pattern on KV prefetch in canary after the CUDA 13.3 driver + cuDNN bump. Smallbatch (seq=16, batch=4) on A100. ci-bot flagged ~+12% p99 across runs. Repro script attached below.

ci-bot: perf/regression detected: runtime-smallbatch-canary job -> smallbatch_p99 +12% vs baseline. Job: build/rt-smallbatch/187. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/rt-smallbatch/187 :warning:

kai: @tess can you paste the kernel selection logs and nvprof snippet? sounds like a kernel flip rather than pure bandwidth issue.

mike: quick note — this matches the pattern we saw with the cuDNN algo chooser flip last year (kernel_v3 selected over kernel_v1 for certain tile sizes). Could be autotune table reshuffle after driver change.

tess: pasted quick log excerpt: ```KernelDispatch: matmul_128x128_tiled selected kernel_v3 (score=0.78) previously kernel_v1 (score=1.12) | exec_time_v3=1.82ms exec_time_v1=1.18ms | L2_rd=+34% L2_wr=+22%```

sophie: nvprof perf counters show increased L2 traffic and higher DRAM utilization when kernel_v3 is used. sm_eff roughly stable, but memory-bound path runtime increases. Looks like matmul tiling changed kernel memory access pattern.

kai: repro attempts? can we run on perf rig and try forcing kernel_v1 to verify improvement? also check Triton version — did the triton autotune table format bump?

mike: ran a quick image with triton pinned to 2.6.0 (we've got 2.6.1 in the canary image). Pin to 2.6.0 -> p99 drops back to baseline. So plausible interaction: CUDA13.3 driver + Triton 2.6.1 autotune/resolution yields different selector scores.

tess: repro script (run on perf rig): ```./perf/repro_smallbatch.sh --model gptj --seq 16 --batch 4 --log-kernels --force-kernel=auto``` Also autotune cache path note: /var/tmp/triton_autotune/13.3/registry.json contains new heuristic weights.

ci-bot: issue created: PT-4827 "KV prefetch sawtooth after CUDA13.3 + Triton 2.6.1". Labels: perf, regression, rollout-blocker. Linked PRs: #9123 (driver bump), #9188 (triton bump).

sophie: extra data: perf counter dump: ```L2_read_transactions=1.34e6 L2_write_transactions=4.2e5 DRAM_bytes=3.1GB sm_eff=0.72 occupancy=0.63``` When forcing kernel_v1: ```L2_read_transactions=9.1e5 DRAM_bytes=2.0GB p99 down ~13%```

mike: short-term plan: pin Triton to 2.6.0 and driver 13.2 on canary; start rolling out revert ASAP. Longer term: update selector to include memory-bandwidth cost term and add a perf-regression unit test that runs smallbatch + autotune and alerts on kernel-choice changes that increase latency >5%.

kai: I'll run a bisect across triton autotune table commits and driver microversions. If autoscore is deterministic, we can identify the change in weight scaling that flipped to kernel_v3. Also add a fallback: if selected kernel increases observed p99 >5% compared to cached baseline, fall back to previous variant for N minutes.

tess: rolling revert now to driver 13.2 on canary. I'll post numbers in ~10m. Thanks all. :eyes:

ci-bot: rollback started: canary nodes image -> image-2025-03-12-driver13.2. Watch job: https://ci.internal/redwood/deploy/450 :truck:

mike: filing cleanup tasks: PT-4828 (add autotune unit test), PT-4829 (selector memory-cost), PT-4830 (fallback kernel variant on latency spike).

tess: confirmed — after rollback p99 back to baseline within noise (~+1%). I'll leave monitoring on for 2h then mark PT-4827 with postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
